{
  "signals_observed": [
    "Alert date: 2024-10-09; merchant_id: 135.",
    "Trigger B: AUP-06.1 breach: 30d chargeback rate 5.0% (3 disputes / 60 orders).",
    "cb_rate_30d: 0.05; disputes_30d: 3; orders_30d: 60.",
    "volume_z: 0.2626128657194451; ticket_drift: 1.0430172732449523.",
    "gmv_30d: 540015 cents; base_gmv: 1501455 cents over base_days: 90.",
    "base_orders: 174; base_mu: 1.9333333333333333.",
    "new_gmv_30d: 82073 cents; new_gmv_share: 0.1519828152921678.",
    "refunds_30d: 0; refund_rate_30d: 0.0; base_refunds: 0; base_refund_rate: 0.0.",
    "merchant_age_days: 190; cum_orders: 383."
  ],
  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "kind": "bustout",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "The dispute-rate breach warrants investigation, but volume_z and ticket_drift do not indicate a pronounced sales or ticket ramp. Non-delivery, thin buyer accounts and settlement extraction are not established by these metrics."
    },
    {
      "kind": "marketing_push",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "A campaign could produce legitimate orders with fulfillment or customer-service problems, but no campaign evidence is supplied. The volume metrics provide little support for a substantial marketing-driven spike."
    },
    {
      "kind": "data_issue",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "Three disputes divided by 60 orders matches the reported 5.0%, so there is no visible arithmetic inconsistency. Duplicate disputes, incomplete order ingestion or mismatched event windows still require reconciliation."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "reserve",
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "Review the three dispute records for reason, status, transaction linkage and supporting evidence. Corroborated non-delivery would strengthen the bust-out concern; resolved service issues or invalid records would weaken it.",
    "Check fulfillment evidence for disputed orders and a small sample of recent high-value orders: carrier acceptance, delivery confirmation or applicable service-completion records. Verify selected records independently.",
    "Reconcile the reported zero refunds against refund requests, cancellations and processor records. Unprocessed requests alongside missing fulfillment would increase concern.",
    "Request campaign dates, offer terms and order-source records to test whether legitimate promotion explains affected sales and whether fulfillment kept pace.",
    "Reconcile the 60 orders and three disputes with source records, checking completeness, duplicates and window definitions. Confirm what 'new_gmv' measures before interpreting it as buyer-account risk."
  ],
  "memo_markdown": "Merchant 135 breached AUP-06.1 on 2024-10-09: three disputes across 60 trailing-30-day orders produce a 5.0% reported chargeback rate. GMV was 540,015 cents. Volume_z was 0.263 and ticket_drift was 1.043; neither shows a pronounced ramp. Reported refunds were zero, which does not establish successful fulfillment.\n\nRecommend a provisional payout reserve for human approval while reviewing the disputed transactions. The breach warrants exposure protection, but these metrics alone do not corroborate bust-out or justify offboarding.\n\nPrioritize dispute reasons and supporting records, independently verifiable fulfillment, and reconciliation of refund requests with processor activity. Check campaign records and reconcile dispute/order counts with source data. Repeated verified non-delivery, unresolved refund requests and continued payout extraction would strengthen the concern and support considering a settlement pause. Verified delivery, explained disputes, or corrected source counts would weaken it and support returning to monitoring. Campaign evidence helps explain sales only when fulfillment is also verified."
}
